heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

1. Region is Wonosobo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Wonosobo.
4. Vice Regent is the Vice Regent of Wonosobo.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Wonosobo Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Apparatus of Wonosobo Regency tasked in the field of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children.
7. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD is part of SKPD.
8. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions.
9. Social welfare administration for women and children is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Government, Regional Government and society in the form of social services to meet the basic needs of every citizen, especially women and children, which includes social rehabilitation, social security, social empowerment, and social protection.
10. Social problems.
11. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life.
12. Social empowerment is all efforts directed to make citizens experiencing social problems have power, so that they are able to meet their basic needs.
13. Social security is an institutionalized scheme to ensure all people can meet their basic needs for a decent life.
14. Social protection is all efforts directed to prevent and handle risks from social problems.
15. Special protection is.
16. Social outreach is a series of activities to pick up women and children who are in parks, markets, streets and public places that can cause social problems, so that these women and children receive social welfare administration services.
17. Social organization is a social association formed by the community that is legally incorporated or not legally incorporated that functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare efforts.
18. Social Institution is an institution or work unit established by the community and or government that provides social welfare services.
19. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (Eighteen) years old including a child still in the womb.
20. Child in emergency situation is.
21. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly met both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially.
22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and or mental障碍 so that their growth and development is disrupted properly.
23. Child welfare is a child's life that can guarantee their growth and development properly both physically, spiritually and socially.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
25. Poor family is a family that does not have a source of livelihood and does not have the ability to meet basic needs that are decent for humanity or people who have a source of livelihood but cannot meet decent basic needs.
26. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
27. Human trafficking is.
28. Victim is.
29. Person with disability is every person who has physical and or mental abnormalities that can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to perform properly consisting of persons with physical and mental disabilities.
30. Social deviant is a person whose life does not conform to religious norms, moral norms, legal norms, and or community norms.
31. Care is various efforts given to children who do not have parents and are neglected, neglected children, and children experiencing behavioral problems, which are temporary in nature as a substitute for parents or family so that they can grow and develop properly both spiritually, physically, and socially.
32. Social assistance is assistance that is not permanent or temporary and is given within a certain period of time to social welfare beneficiaries who are unable so that they can improve their social welfare level and are able to carry out their social functions properly in community life both spiritually, physically, and socially.
33. Community members are residents of Wonosobo Regency and foreign citizens living in Wonosobo Regency.
34. Society is a group of community members who have interest and role in the field of social welfare.
35. Violence against children is.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

SCOPE

Article 2

The scope of social protection includes: women and children with social problems.

heading: Article 3
Article 4
translated_text:
Article 4

Social protection for women and children in the form of:
a. Social assistance;
b. Social advocacy; and/or
c. legal aid.

heading: CHAPTER III
Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

Social protection for women and children functions to:
a. prevent the emergence, growth and development of social welfare problems.
b. restore social functions in achieving independence.
c. increase community social resilience in preventing and handling social welfare problems.
d. develop social potential.
e. empower social resources.
f. prevent social vulnerability.

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children.
c. improve the level of welfare, quality, and survival.
d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence.
e. increase community social resilience in preventing and handling social welfare problems.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world in the administration of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business world and society.

CHAPTER IV

Part One

General

Article 9
Article 10

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Social Protection and Social Welfare Administration for Women

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

Every Woman has the right to obtain social protection in the form of equal treatment and opportunities in education and training, work protection for safety and/or health concerning women's reproductive function in accordance with decent norms of life and livelihood.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

Every woman is obliged to maintain her dignity and that of her family as well as her nature as a woman by taking into account her function and role in family and/or community life in accordance with her abilities.

heading: Article 16
Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

Every institution, both government and private, that organizes public services or employs women must provide adequate facilities for the interests of women.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Social Protection and Social Welfare Administration for Children

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. Every child has the right to receive social protection and social welfare administration from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop normally.
2. Every child has the right to receive social protection and social welfare administration to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become good and useful members of society.
3. Every child has the right to receive maintenance of child welfare standards and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development normally.
4. Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, mistreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and mental social guidance.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. Everyone is prohibited from neglecting, committing acts of violence and/or exploitation against children.
2. Everyone is prohibited from employing children under working age as regulated in the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

The regional government and/or community may carry out social protection and social welfare administration for children for the purpose of improving child welfare carried out in accordance with statutory provisions.

heading: Article 21

heading: Article 22

translated_text:
Article 23

1. In carrying out the responsibility as referred to in Article 21 paragraph (3), SKPD/UKPD shall prepare a plan for social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children.
2. In preparing the plan as referred to in paragraph (2), it shall be guided by the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJM) and the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJP).
3. The plan for implementation of social welfare as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

The role of business entities as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) letter g in social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children shall be carried out as part of social and environmental responsibility in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

The regional government may grant awards to the community, social organizations and business entities that play a role in social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children.

heading: Article 28
CHAPTER VI

translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Part One

Guidance

heading: Article 30
Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

1. Coordination as referred to in Article 30 letter a shall begin from the planning, implementation and evaluation stages.
2. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented at the regency, sub-district and village levels by SKPD/UKPD.

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. Establishment of guidelines and standards as referred to in Article 30 letter b shall cover planning, implementation, procedures, funding, quality, control and supervision.
2. Establishment of guidelines and standards as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be prepared by SKPD/UKPD.

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. Provision of counseling, guidance, supervision, and consultation as referred to in Article 30 letter c shall cover planning, implementation, procedures, funding, quality, control and supervision.
2. Counseling and/or guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be directed to the community, social organizations and business entities. (3) Provision of counseling, guidance, supervision, and consultation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by SKPD/UKPD.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

1. Research, monitoring and evaluation as referred to in Article 30 letter d shall be conducted in the context of evaluating the social impact of development, policy development and achievement of social welfare objectives.
2. Research, monitoring, and evaluation shall be implemented periodically or according to needs by SKPD/UKPD in accordance with their functions and authorities.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Supervision

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

1. The regional government shall conduct supervision over social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with the principles of transparency and accountability.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. Functional supervision over social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children shall be implemented by functional supervisory officials.
2. Technical operational supervision over social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children organized by social organizations and the community shall be conducted by SKPD/UKPD.
3. Further provisions regarding the implementation of supervision shall be regulated by Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

1. Social organizations and or the community may participate in conducting supervision over social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in accordance with the laws and regulations

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 38

1. Every social organization that has obtained a permit in the implementation of social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children, which deliberately does not provide social services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (5), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
2. Every social organization that implements social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children without a permit as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (6), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. revocation of permit.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 39

1. Any person who neglects, commits acts of violence and/or exploitation against children as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 77 letter b, Article 80, Article 81, Article 82, and Article 88 of Law No. 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
2. Any person who employs children under working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

INVESTIGATION

Article 40

Investigation may be carried out by Civil Servant Investigators (PPNS) within the Regional Government.

heading: Article 41
CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 42

All provisions relating to social protection and the implementation of social welfare for women and children that existed before the promulgation of this Regional Regulation, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 43

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Wonosobo Regency.

Enacted in Wonosobo

on 26 March 2012

heading: I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed at Women and Children. Especially programs to improve the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide studies within a philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in an effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must pay attention to environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that have the potential to harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in the matter of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

heading: Article 3

translated_text:
Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years who behaves in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking a livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities normally, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, persons with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable to socio-economic conditions is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment

heading: Article 5

translated_text:
Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people in need of assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of the child, birth order of the child, and physical and mental condition.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.
